summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Solaris Health through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Key focuses: per-route cost attribution, model routing policy, batching/caching impact on unit cost, and security requirements for Private deployment. Agreed next steps: pricing deck, SOC2 + KMS docs, sample prompt sets for pilot.
questions: How does per-route attribution work with mixed-model routing?
What visibility do we get into token-level cost and latency?
How is customer data isolated in Private deployment?
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood Inference - i run the east accounts, along with elena our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya: hey, doing good, thanks. excited to see the console walkthrough. we've been trying to get a clearer sense for per-route costs, and how routing affects our overall bill.
[00:13] Liam: yeah quick intro, our main goal is to embed summarization + clinical QA into our provider portal, and we need predictable cost and low tail latency.
[00:20] Elena: great, we'll start in the Console and focus on the Usage Analytics page — i'll show per-route dashboards, token level breakdowns, and the cost calc. FYI there might be a couple small audio glitches, transcription isn't perfect.
[00:29] Maya: loud and clear here.
[00:32] [00:32] Elena: (screen share) ok, so this is the home view: topline usage, errors, and model mix. you can filter by route, model, or time window. here we have a route called "clinical-summarize" and one called "qa-session".
[00:45] Priya: can i see cost by route?
[00:46] Elena: yes — click the route and there's a per-route dashboard. you'll get tokens in/out, latency distribution, p50/p95/p99 and a cost line that shows compute + storage (kv cache) and network where applicable.
[00:58] Samir: one thing to call out, the cost breakdown is unitized — we show per-token compute adjusted by model and quantization, plus any specialized ops (like long-context kernels), and a small storage/KV cache cost for prefix caching.
[01:12] Liam: ok how does routing factor when we do fallback to a cheaper model? does the per-route cost reflect mixed-model usage?
[01:19] Elena: good question — yes, the per-route attribution is request-based. if a request hits model A for generation and falls back to model B, the dashboard attributes the cost to the route and shows the split by model. there can be slight attribution delay (a few minutes) if you have high throughput.
[01:33] [01:33] Priya: (murmur) that split is important, we need to show finance that the canary doesn't blow up costs.
[01:38] Elena: absolutely. also we surface the batching efficiency. if you look at the route details there's a batching slider and a histogram that shows observed batch sizes vs ideal — you can simulate increased batching and see predicted unit cost reduction.
[01:52] Samir: another lever is KV/prefix caching. for example our clinical-summarize route sees lots of repeated patient context, caching the KV reduces generation tokens and latency, which you can see in the KPI.
[02:04] Maya: how is KV stored for Private? encrypted?
[02:06] Elena: yes for Private we integrate with customer KMS — the cache is encrypted at rest. key rotation supported via KMS, same for model artifacts in the private control plane.
[02:16] Liam: what about telemetry and audit logs — do we get per-request traces?
[02:20] Samir: we provide tracing hooks and per-token latency breakdowns; audit logs cover API calls, route changes, and rollout events. we can retain logs longer for enterprise add-on.
[02:31] [02:31] Priya: can you show an example of cost calc?
[02:34] Elena: sure; under Cost Insights there's a cost simulator. i'll pick the clinical-summarize route — current split: 70% hosted gpt-ish open model (we'll call it r-7b), 30% fallback to r-13b for long context. projected monthly spend is shown with live qps and average prompt length. if we enable batching to target 4 per batch and enable kv cache, unit cost drops about 35% in this example.
[02:58] Liam: big drop — do you have the math exported?
[03:01] Elena: yes you can export a CSV and a slide-ready cost breakdown. i'll attach that after.
[03:08] Priya: what's the delta between hosted and Dedicated numbers? at our scale we care about predictability.
[03:14] Samir: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; cost per token usually decreases because of reserved capacity and better packing. the console shows both equivalent projections — for dedicated we model committed instances and compute amortization.
[03:28] Maya: does dedicated support burst capacity? sometimes our traffic spikes during intake windows.
[03:31] Elena: yes, there's configurable burst policies. you set baseline capacity and a burst buffer; the console will simulate burst costs as well.
[03:39] [03:39] Priya: security: we need SOC2 and ISO, and SSO/SAML for RBAC — can you confirm?
[03:44] Samir: yes SOC2 Type II; ISO in progress; SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC in Console. i'll send the compliance pack.
[03:53] Liam: any concerns about data residency? we need EU-only for some customers.
[03:57] Elena: we support region pins and private control plane for VPC — you can force routing to a region or have the private deployment entirely in your VPC.
[04:07] Priya: on the per-route dashboard, can we annotate routes with business tags for finance?
[04:11] Elena: yes tags and cost centers — you can map routes to charge codes and export attribution by cost center.
[04:18] [04:18] Samir: quick aside — one common misconception is that quantization always reduces cost with no quality impact; for clinical QA you want to test. we can recommend quantization profiles per model and run evaluations against your prompt set.
[04:30] Priya: that's a must for us, we can't have hallucinations on clinical parts.
[04:33] Elena: totally — we have a quality monitoring feature: you upload prompt/eval sets and we run periodic regression checks, tie alerts to rollouts.
[04:42] Liam: can we do a pilot with private deployment + limited hosted fallback?
[04:46] Samir: yes hybrid is common — private control plane + on-prem model execution for sensitive routes, with hosted for lower-sensitivity workloads.
[04:54] Maya: what does the integration look like — how much infra work?
[04:56] Elena: for Private there's an agent and a deployment manifest; typical on-prem install is 2-3 weeks if you have infra resources, less if we co-manage. for the short pilot we can run a sandbox dedicated instance with a sample dataset.
[05:10] [05:10] Priya: timeline wise we want pilot done before end of sept, decision by mid-oct.
[05:14] Samir: noted — that's doable. we'll send a suggested pilot plan.
[05:18] Elena: back to the console — here's the per-request table, you can click into an individual request to see the full token trace: prompt tokens, model selected, kv hits, and response tokens, and the cost calc for that request.
[05:31] Priya: helpful. does that table expose PII? we need to mask PHI in logs.
[05:36] Elena: you can redact sensitive fields before sending, and we have a field-level masking option for logs — the default retention for hosted doesn't store full prompt by default for regulated customers.
[05:48] Liam: what about anomaly detection on cost? like unexpected burst or runaway prompts?
[05:52] Samir: we have alerting rules tied to routes and cost thresholds. you can set notification channels and auto-throttle or fallback on breach.
[05:59] [05:59] Maya: on the billing export, is the model inference cost broken down per GPU type?
[06:03] Elena: yes the export includes model variant, underlying hardware class, and token-level compute cost; so you can see e.g., r-13b on p4 vs r-7b on a100.
[06:14] Priya: ok, curious about the sample numbers you showed earlier — can you run that same calc with our actual prompts?
[06:19] Elena: absolutely, if you share a representative set we'll run a benchmark and give a cost-sensitivity report.
[06:24] Samir: we'll also include a few routing recommendations: model mix, batching targets, and cache TTL suggestions.
[06:30] [06:30] Priya: fine — i'll share 2 weeks worth of anonymized transcripts.
[06:34] Liam: and we'll need contract language for data handling.
[06:36] Samir: yep, legal will follow.
[06:39] Elena: last part — the Console has a Rollouts page. you can do canary %s, automated rollback on quality regressions, and link rollouts to the eval sets. this prevents noisy rollouts that spike costs.
[06:53] Priya: that auto rollback on quality drop is appealing.
[06:56] Samir: ok let me recap next steps, we will: 1) send pricing deck and pilot proposal (Samir), 2) bench with your prompts and export cost sims (Elena), 3) provide SOC2 + private deployment checklist and compliance pack (Samir/Elena), 4) customer to share prompts and confirm pilot timeline (Priya/Liam).
[07:18] [07:18] Priya: sounds good.
[07:20] Liam: thanks, helpful session.
[07:22] Samir: thanks everyone, i'll email the assets and follow up with a calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
[07:27] Elena: thanks all.
[07:29] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
